title: On the limitations of molecular representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.08420v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. We carried out a systematic investigation of the quality of molecular representations, finding that none of the state-of-the-art molecular embedding models capture graph structure, 3D shape, or ADMET endpoint similarity better than fingerprints or physicochemical descriptors. However, classical fingerprints also revealed their own material limitations. For example, we show that depending on the representation, between 225M and $\sim$4B molecules have non-unique representations in the 10.8B Enamine REAL database, with implications for virtual screening. tldr: 本文系统评估了分子表示方法的质量，发现最先进的分子嵌入模型在捕捉图结构、3D形状和ADMET相似性方面均不及传统指纹与理化描述符，且经典指纹自身也存在严重局限——在大规模数据库中可导致高达数十亿分子的表示不唯一，影响虚拟筛选的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This systematic study shows that state-of-the-art molecular embedding models do not outperform classical fingerprints or physicochemical descriptors at capturing graph structure, 3D shape, or ADMET similarity, while classical fingerprints themselves suffer from serious limitations, such as non-unique representations for hundreds of millions to billions of molecules in large-scale databases.
